posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Where did the antimatter go? The Big Bang should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which would have annihilated each other instantly. So why does anything exist at all? Scientists are still hunting for the missing half of reality.

What we know about human history is only a fraction of the full story. Much of the rest is like dark matter, invisible to us. We can’t see it, and we can only see the effects of its presence. But thanks to new techniques for DNA sequencing, dating ancient detritus, mathematical models, and aerial and lidar archaeology, we are now able to get a faint idea of what this world might have looked and felt like.

Have you ever heard of the Blue People of the Sahara? ⁠
⁠
They’re the Tuareg, a traditionally nomadic people of North and West Africa whose culture has lasted for centuries.⁠
⁠
@visualsbyponzio captured their beauty and traditions in Mali, from the striking tagelmust and handcrafted silver jewelry to the tehardent, a traditional lute that keeps their stories alive.⁠
⁠
The indigo dye of their veils rubs off on the skin, which is how they earned their famous nickname, “Blue People”. They also call

In Monroe, Louisiana, two buildings from 1891 that once held an opera house and a grocery store are now the first certified 100% gluten-free hotel in the US. ⁠
⁠
Certified by the Gluten-Free Food Program and endorsed by the National Celiac Association, it serves a fully gluten-free menu across its restaurant, rooftop bar, room service, and events. ⁠
⁠
Tag a friend who’s always checking the menu for gluten-free options 🍽️⁠
⁠
By: @thehotelmonroe

Who says a dog and owls can’t be best friends? 🦉🐶⁠
⁠
Award-winning photographer @tanja_brandt has spent years capturing the unlikely bond between her dog and owls, and these photos prove friendship comes in all shapes and sizes.⁠
⁠
Which photo melted your heart the most??

Autumn really knows how to show off 🍁⁠
⁠
@motaz_azaiza captured the season from above, where every tree turns its own shade of red, orange, gold, or green, and quiet roads wind through the colors.⁠
⁠
Which slide is your favorite? ⁠

German photographer Christian Vieler, who is world-renowned for his dog photography, turned his camera to senior dogs, and the result is pure warmth. ⁠
⁠
Each portrait shows a dog who has slowed down a little but hasn’t lost any of their spark. ⁠
⁠⁠
Which photo is your favorite?!⁠
⁠
By: @vieler.photography

A bar where you get great beer and a few slaps and kicks from the Muscle Girls? 🍺😂 ⁠
This unusual experience combines a night out with some playful sparring from strong women, making it a bar visit you definitely won’t forget.⁠
⁠
Would you try it, or stick to just the beer? 👀⁠
🎥: @ngtnz

Harry Potter fans know this bridge as the route to Hogwarts, but the Glenfinnan Viaduct was carrying trains across the Scottish Highlands long before the films. ⁠
⁠
Opened in 1901, it was built from mass concrete with no steel inside, and its 21 arches stretch about 381 meters above the River Finnan.⁠
⁠
Every year from June to October, the Jacobite steam train travels between Fort William and Mallaig, crossing the viaduct along the way. ⁠
⁠

Have you ever seen a bird with sunflower-like eyes? 🌻⁠
⁠
These birds are white-crested Helmetshrikes, and that bright yellow “sunflower” is actually a skin structure called a wattle that only adults have.⁠
⁠
They are as social as they are striking. They live in close-knit groups that can stay together for years, and the whole group helps raise the chicks.⁠
⁠
By: @veronicadonoso_b

No traffic lights, no problem! ⁠
In Thimphu, the capital of Bhutan, traffic is directed by police officers using hand signals from a small decorative booth instead of automated lights. 🚦⁠
⁠
The city once tried traffic lights, but they were eventually removed in favor of human traffic control. A unique sight that makes you look twice when exploring Bhutan!⁠
🎥: @thecubancarrie

Artist @simonorourke turned a storm-damaged tree into a giant hand reaching for the sky.⁠
⁠
Once the tallest tree in Wales, it was due to be cut down after a storm left it damaged. ⁠
⁠
Simon turned it into a memorial for the much-loved landmark, known as "Giant Hand of Vyrnwy."⁠
⁠

@amiina_abroad discovers a restaurant in Thailand where getting through the entrance can save you money! 😂⁠
⁠
The restaurant has different-sized gates, and the one you manage to squeeze through determines your discount, ranging from 5% to 20%. A pretty unusual way to welcome customers and add a little challenge before the meal even begins! 🍜👀⁠
⁠
Which gate do you think you’d make it through?

Keeping up with a pack of hunting wolves is just another day at the office for @bertiegregory and his team.

#WolvesUpClose with Bertie Gregory premieres Friday, November 6 at 8/7c on National Geographic. Streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Presented by National Geographic Society in partnership with @Rolex. In the face of a changing world, these explorers are not giving up hope for our seas. Narrated by @auliicravalho, set sail across all five ocean basins in Expedition: Saving Our Seas, premiering Friday, November 13 at 9/8c on @natgeotv. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Rolex and The National Geographic Society are partnering on science-based expeditions to explore, study, and document change in the planet’s unique

Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Photographer @arkodatto captured this striking image of a home sitting atop a ruined embankment on Mousuni Island—where cyclones, monsoons, and rising sea levels are reshaping life in India’s Sundarbans. The damage affects millions of residents, many of whom rely on local agriculture for employment. As these impacts grow, some are migrating elsewhere.

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

Thinking about taking part in Sober October? 🚫🍷

It might only be a month, but it can have a huge impact. According to researchers, within mere weeks of giving up alcohol, the liver begins to regenerate, mood improves, and participants notice healthier skin and better sleep, among other health benefits.

Find out more about what happens to your mental and physical health when you give up alcohol at the link in bio.

Photograph by Victoria Jones, PA Images/Getty Images

Presented by @Rolex. Filmed over 4 years across 32 countries, Africa's wild landscape tells one story—but the numbers reveal another one altogether. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

What would a diver really face inside the ocean’s largest toothed predator? Whalefall's director and co-screenwriter, @briancduffield, and author and co-screenwriter, Daniel Kraus (@kraus_author), sat down with whale biologist @shanegero, National Geographic Explorer and Field Biology Lead of @projectceti, to unpack the real biology behind this larger-than-life story.

Watch #Whalefall, only in theaters, and stream these National Geographic shows and more on @DisneyPlus.

Mobula rays sail through the water in the Sea of Cortez, off the coast of Baja California, which is a fertile feeding ground for them. Photographer Martin Greguš Jr. (@mywildlive) filmed this group using a drone, noting that from above, it felt more like watching a flock of birds flying through the sky.

A yellow-legged gull stands alongside its painted counterpart in Rome. Captured by @gianlucadamiani_photographer, the photograph was a winning entry in the 2026 Bird Photographer of the Year competition. These birds have made themselves right at home in the city, using tall buildings to nest and perch. During the COVID-19 pandemic, residents even left pet food on ledges, helping the gulls thrive alongside people.

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

One in seven adults will fall victim to a romance scam. To uncover the world of these predators, @marianavz had to become their prey. 

#SuperScamMe is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

The giant anteater population in Brazil is declining due to an increase in roadside collisions, with 766 of the elusive creatures found dead along highways in Mato Grosso do Sul from 2017 to 2020, including this one that was struck by a vehicle. To document the threats facing giant anteaters, National Geographic Explorer and photographer @fernando.faciole spent years following the species, splitting his time between the roads and rehabilitation centers.
